subject: Production spike: sudden p95/p99 latency regression & throughput drop (FastCommerce)
messages:
From: Samira Kahn <samira.kahn@fastcommerce.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike — p95/p99 up, throughput falling

Hi Marcus / Laura / Monica,

We're seeing a sudden degradation in our Redwood-hosted API traffic starting ~07:50 PST. Key symptoms:
- p95 increased from ~180ms to ~1.2s; p99 jumped to ~2.4s
- overall TPS dropped ~45% despite request rate holding steady
- error rate bumped to 1.6% (mostly 504 timeouts)

This started abruptly; we haven't pushed any changes. Our ops alerts show a correlated drop in prefix cache hit rate (was ~92% at 07:45, dropped to ~18% by 07:55). Attaching a screenshot of our dashboard.

This is impacting checkout flows on our peak region. Can you confirm if this is an infrastructure change or a cache invalidation event on Redwood's side? We need an ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Samira Kahn
Head of Platform Ops, FastCommerce
ops@fastcommerce.com

Attachment: p95-regression-graphs.png (image/PNG)

Thanks for the heads up, Samira — and sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as SEV-2 until we have more context. Immediate next steps:
1) I'm escalating to SRE and Eng (looping Rishi and Tessa).
2) Monica, can you surface the customer's detailed request traces and any recent model variant fallbacks?
3) Laura, please coordinate communication and let the customer know we're on it with an initial ETA of 30 min.

We're seeing a similar alert on our end (Paging alert INF-7312). Preliminary telemetry shows a rapid decline in prefix/KV cache hit ratio on the hosted pools serving FastCommerce. I'm starting a cache-dump and will attach logs.

Samira — really sorry this hit you during a busy window. We're assembling a short mutual action plan so you know exactly what's happening and when we'll have mitigations in place. Draft below: 

Mutual Action Plan (short)
- 08:35: SRE will confirm whether this is a cache invalidation cascade or a broader KV outage.
- 08:45: If eviction/miss storm confirmed, enable temporary fallback routing to cached model variant (same family, slightly wider latency envelope).
- 09:00: Run targeted KV warmup and prefix-prefetch for FastCommerce hot keys.
- 09:30: Post-mitigation verification (p95/p99 and error rate).

I'll keep the customer updated every 30 minutes. Marcus / Engineering: please advise on whether automatic fallback is safe for this customer and whether we can increase prefix TTL briefly.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — p95/p99 up, throughput falling

Assigning INF-7312 to Eng. This looks like a classic prefix-cache miss storm — likely caused by an unexpected purge or TTL regression on one of the hosted pools. Immediately:
- Tessa: please validate whether a config push or maintenance job touched prefix eviction parameters for pools us-west-2-prod-1 around 07:40–08:00.
- Ops: enable fallback to model-variant:v2-cacheable for routes serving FastCommerce (rollback path ready).
- Marcus: collect heap traces + kv proxy logs and attach to the Jira ticket.

I'll join the call if this needs exec attention. If we confirm a purge on our side, flag to legal/CS for potential SLA credits and prepare a short exec brief.

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — p95/p99 up, throughput falling

Status update: we confirmed an automated maintenance job that trimmed prefix TTLs in us-west-2-prod-1 at 07:41 (config diff attached). The chain of events: TTL trim -> rapid prefix evictions -> cache miss storm -> KV proxy contention -> increased tail latency and upstream timeouts.

Actions taken so far:
- Rolled back TTL change at 08:55 PST.
- Enabled fallback routing to model-variant:v2-cacheable for FastCommerce routes at 09:00 PST.
- Running a KV warmup script against identified hot prefixes (started 09:02 PST).

Attached: prefix-cache-dump.tar.gz (contains sampled kvproxy logs and prefix list), short traces. Initial telemetry shows cache-hit % recovering (from 18% -> 67% over 20 minutes) and p95 trending down.

I'll continue to push updates. Laura — please update FastCommerce with current ETA for stabilization (we expect positive improvement within 30–45 minutes).

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Incident update & next steps — INF-7312 (FastCommerce)

Final status (summary):
- Root cause: automated TTL adjustment in maintenance job for us-west-2-prod-1 caused widespread prefix evictions and a subsequent KV miss storm.
- Impact window: ~07:50–09:25 PST. During the peak, FastCommerce saw p95/p99 regressions and a ~45% drop in throughput.
- Remediation: rolled back TTL change (08:55 PST), enabled variant fallback (09:00 PST), completed targeted kv warmup (09:20 PST). Observed p95 near-baseline by 09:40 PST and error rates returned to normal.
- Action items:
  1) Ops: add a safety check to maintenance jobs that modify prefix TTLs (INF-7320).
  2) Eng: implement a graceful degraded-mode that uses local cache snapshot when eviction rates spike (design doc due 2026-12-01).
  3) CS/Legal: prepare customer-facing RCA and SLA credit worksheet.

Laura — I attached the mutual-action-plan doc and export of the logs for your packet. Recommend a short RCA call tomorrow (Nov 16) 09:00 PST to walk FastCommerce through the timeline and remediation.

Thanks again for patience, Samira — we'll follow up with a formal RCA and credit worksheet shortly.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.docx, prefix-cache-dump.tar.gz

—Marcus
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
